draft.headline: Paris has been South Africa's ground since 2013
beats: South Africa have beaten France five straight times at the Stade de France since 2013, the last of them 32–17 on 8 November 2025. France lead the North and South Africa the South, which is exactly the pairing for the grand final. Paris may only be the rehearsal.
Both arrive warm. France ran in eight tries past Fiji, 54–17. South Africa ran in nine past Italy, 66–7, and Erasmus says half his squad has hardly been worked.

His one change to the starting side is Wilco Louw at tighthead, picked for his scrummaging, beside Ox Nche and Malcolm Marx. Erasmus calls France one of "the teams that maul the most", and has answered with weight.
A France win would lift them to 3rd in the world and drop South Africa to 2nd, below New Zealand. It has not happened in Paris since 2013.

draft.headline: Italy have lost five straight; one win makes them ninth
beats: Italy have conceded 66, 57 and 47 in their last three Nations Championship games, and are last of twelve without a point. Beat Argentina in Genoa and they still climb from 11th to 9th in the world, above Fiji and Wales.

Argentina arrive short of hookers and fullbacks. Julián Montoya failed an HIA in the 42–12 loss in Dublin and Leonel Oviedo is in doubt, so Facundo Bosch is back in the squad for the first time since 2021. With the senior fullbacks hurt, back-up fly-half Gerónimo Prisciantelli may start at 15.
Danilo Fischetti summed up the mood swing: after England, Italy were the best side in the world; two defeats later, the worst. He wants a reaction in performance first, results second.
Argentina have won once in seven Tests this year. Italy have faced worse odds, most recently against South Africa.

issues.claim: Facundo Bosch is back in the squad for the first time since 2021
issues.problem: The pack says only that Bosch's most recent cap was in 2021 under Mario Ledesma. It does not say he has been out of the squad since then or that this is his first call-up since 2021. The 'first time since' framing is an unsupported claim.
issues.fix: Facundo Bosch joins the squad as a hooker; his most recent Argentina cap came in 2021.

draft.headline: Rees-Zammit is smiling at a record that goes back to 1953
beats: Wales have beaten New Zealand three times in 38 Tests, the last in 1953. Louis Rees-Zammit was player of the match against Japan, with 14 defenders beaten, and says he is "playing with a smile on my face".

The smile has history to get past. The last meeting, in Cardiff on 22 November 2025, finished 26–52. New Zealand have since put 43 on Australia and 43 on Scotland, seven tries each time. Wales needed hard work to beat Japan 28–21 in Cardiff and were held scoreless in South Africa in July.

New Zealand may be without Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan, both hurt at Murrayfield. They are level on points with South Africa, with only points difference between them, so the margin in Cardiff matters to them as well as the result.
A Wales win would lift them to ninth, above Fiji. Fiji would be the second-most surprised party.

draft.headline: England's two-try wing is needed back in the back row
beats: Henry Pollock came off the bench against Australia and scored twice on the wing. Steve Borthwick has suggested he is unlikely to start there against Japan, because the back row is running short: Tom Curry is out for November, with Guy Pepper and Sam Underhill also unavailable.

The 45-22 cost more than it looked. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's ankle ends his autumn, and three more first-choice players spend this week rehabbing in camp with one eye on New Zealand next weekend. Borthwick needs three new starters in the backline and a blindside.

Japan lost 21-28 in Cardiff on 7 November, trailing by seven at half-time and losing by seven at the end. They are also the reigning Pacific Nations Cup champions after beating Fiji 20-15 in the final. Beat England by 16 or more and Scotland go above them in the world rankings.
England have never lost to Japan in six meetings. The side asked to keep that going will be built partly from whoever is left.

issues.claim: Beat beyond the headline: "Beat England by 16 or more and Scotland go above them in the world rankings."
issues.problem: Wrong team and wrong movement. Per Rankings at stake, a Japan win by 16 or more lifts Japan to 9th, above Fiji, Wales and Italy. It is England who drop to 6th, below Scotland. Scotland does not pass Japan.
issues.fix: Beat England by 16 or more and Japan climb to 9th in the world rankings, while England drop to 6th, below Scotland.

issues.claim: Headline: "England's two-try wing is needed back in the back row"
issues.problem: Presents an expectation as settled fact. The pack says Pollock's move to the back row "could necessitate" his inclusion, and Borthwick has only suggested he is unlikely to start on the wing. No team selection has been announced.
issues.fix: England's two-try wing could be needed back in the back row

Japan lost 21-28 in Cardiff on 7 November, seven behind at half-time and seven behind at the end. They are also the reigning Pacific Nations Cup champions after beating Fiji 20-15 in the final. A Japan win by 16 or more would drop England below Scotland in the world rankings.
England have never lost to Japan in six meetings. The side asked to keep it that way will be built partly from whoever is left.

draft.headline: Three number eights down, and Fiji next
beats: Caelan Doris and Jack Conan were already injured. Sean Jansen, who made his debut against Japan in the summer, went off early in the second half against Argentina and is out for the rest of the championship with a knee injury. Uncapped Ulster forward David McCann has been called up.
The captain has gone too. Dan Sheehan, leading the squad in Doris' absence, is concussed and on a 12-day return-to-play protocol, so Gus McCarthy has been called in to cover at hooker.

Fiji have no points from four Nations Championship games and conceded 54 to France a week earlier. Mack Hansen still warns of a stiff test, and a Fiji win would drop Ireland to 5th in the world, below France and England.
Ireland beat Argentina 42–12 and are still counting what it cost. South Africa come to the Aviva on 21 November, and Andy Farrell would like some forwards left by then.

draft.headline: Australia want a fairer fight. Scotland lost 21–43 too
beats: Planet Rugby's view after the 45–22 defeat at Twickenham is that Scotland are more Australia's level. The scorelines agree. Australia lost 21–43 to New Zealand at home on 17 October, and Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield on 7 November.

Australia have conceded 50, 43 and 45 in their last three games. The Guardian finds them still without an answer at No 10 a year before they host the World Cup. Les Kiss's verdict on England was "We just didn't really fire a shot".
A win of any size takes Australia above Scotland into sixth in the world. Their next game is in Wales, against the side level with Scotland on 10 points in the North.
Scotland also lost 21–43 to Ireland in March. A fairer fight may just mean whoever scores 21 this time doesn't concede 43.
